property.assessed_value.plain: The value your municipality currently places on the taxable land and improvements. It is the assessment basis, not necessarily the property's current sale price.
property.assessed_value.why: This is the starting number for the tax bill and most appeal analysis. It becomes meaningful only when compared with the municipality's assessment ratio and credible market evidence.
property.assessed_value.method: Land assessment plus improvement assessment from the parcel record.
property.assessed_value.caution: Assessed value and market value are different concepts in most New Jersey municipalities.

property.annual_tax.plain: The last full-year property-tax amount reported for this parcel.
property.annual_tax.why: It is the clearest current carrying-cost number, but it does not show whether the property is likely to change after improvements, an added assessment or a municipal revaluation.
property.annual_tax.method: Reported parcel tax for the latest available full year.
property.annual_tax.caution: A seller's current bill is not a guarantee of a buyer's future escrow or tax bill.

watchdog.market_value_estimate.plain: Watchdog's estimate of market value using the parcel assessment and the strongest available municipal assessment-to-market ratio.
watchdog.market_value_estimate.why: It translates a tax assessment into a market-scale number that can support fairness, tax-burden and Chapter 123 analysis.
watchdog.market_value_estimate.method: Assessed value divided by the verified-sales municipal ratio when adequate sales exist; otherwise the published equalization ratio is used.
watchdog.market_value_estimate.caution: This is a screening estimate, not an appraisal or broker price opinion.

sources.label: NJ Division of Taxation verified sales

watchdog.effective_tax_rate.plain: Annual property tax divided by Watchdog's estimated market value, expressed as a percentage.
watchdog.effective_tax_rate.why: Unlike the nominal municipal tax rate, this measure can be compared across towns with different assessment levels.
watchdog.effective_tax_rate.method: Latest full-year parcel tax divided by the supported market-value estimate.
watchdog.effective_tax_rate.caution: The result inherits the limitations of the market-value estimate and is not a forecast of a future bill.

sources.label: NJ Division of Taxation local property tax

watchdog.chapter123_position.plain: Whether the assessment appears above, below or within New Jersey's Chapter 123 common-level range using the current market evidence available to Watchdog.
watchdog.chapter123_position.why: It is the legal screening framework most homeowners and professionals use to decide whether an assessment may be excessive.
watchdog.chapter123_position.method: Compares supported market value with the municipality's common-level ratio and permitted 15% range.
watchdog.chapter123_position.caution: A favorable screen is not a legal conclusion. Filing requires defensible valuation evidence and the current official ratio/range.

uniformity.score.plain: A Watchdog 0–100 translation of how consistently a municipality assesses property, based primarily on New Jersey's coefficient of deviation.
uniformity.score.why: Two towns can use similar assessment ratios but differ greatly in how evenly assessments are distributed. Consistency affects appeal context and confidence in the roll.
uniformity.score.method: Transforms the state-published coefficient of deviation into a statewide comparative score and percentile.
uniformity.score.caution: This describes the municipal roll; it does not by itself decide whether one parcel is correctly assessed.

sources.label: NJ Division of Taxation Coefficients of Deviation

appeals.latest_win_rate_filed.plain: The latest share of filed county tax appeals that ended with an assessment reduction.
appeals.latest_win_rate_filed.why: It provides useful board-level context for evidence standards and outcomes in that county.
appeals.latest_win_rate_filed.method: Assessment-reduction outcomes divided by all filed appeals in the latest published year.
appeals.latest_win_rate_filed.caution: County history is not a prediction for a specific property. Case quality, evidence and procedural compliance matter.

sales.ratio.plain: The median relationship between assessments and sale prices in state-verified arm's-length sales for this municipality.
sales.ratio.why: It provides a market-grounded way to translate assessments and compare properties where assessment levels differ.
sales.ratio.method: Built from usable NJ SR-1A verified sales matched to the municipality.
sales.ratio.caution: Small or unusual sales samples can be less representative; Watchdog requires a minimum sample before using the ratio.

sources.label: NJ Division of Taxation SR-1A sales

sales.ppsf.plain: The median verified sale price per reported square foot in the municipality's usable sales sample.
sales.ppsf.why: It is a quick market context measure and can reveal whether a property estimate is far outside recent local transactions.
sales.ppsf.method: Verified sale price divided by reported building area, summarized as a municipal median.
sales.ppsf.caution: Price per square foot does not adjust for condition, design, lot, location or property subtype.

sources.label: NJ Division of Taxation SR-1A sales

sales.median_price.plain: The midpoint sale price among the municipality's usable state-verified sales.
sales.median_price.why: It places the property in the local transaction market without letting a few unusually high or low sales dominate the result.
sales.median_price.method: Median of usable verified arm's-length sale prices.
sales.median_price.caution: A townwide median is context, not a comparable-market analysis for one house.

sources.label: NJ Division of Taxation SR-1A sales

watchdog.tax_pressure.plain: A Watchdog signal combining municipal levy growth, ratable-base movement, collections, debt and budget balance.
watchdog.tax_pressure.why: Tax rates alone describe the past. Pressure helps identify municipalities where the fiscal ingredients for future increases are accumulating.
watchdog.tax_pressure.method: Weighted model using NJ DCA budget and property-tax components with statewide percentile normalization.
watchdog.tax_pressure.caution: This is an explainable risk indicator, not a forecast of a specific future bill.

watchdog.reassessment_risk.plain: A Watchdog screen for signs that the current assessment may lag a sale, improvement or broader municipal reset.
watchdog.reassessment_risk.why: The current seller's tax bill can understate a future owner's carrying cost when taxable improvements or assessment changes have not fully landed.
watchdog.reassessment_risk.method: Combines sale/assessment relationships, permit and improvement context, added-assessment signals and municipal revaluation pressure when available.
watchdog.reassessment_risk.caution: New Jersey does not generally reassess a property merely because it sold.

sources.label: NJ Division of Taxation local property tax

watchdog.escrow_monthly_delta.plain: The modeled monthly difference between the current tax amount and the user's future-assessment/tax-rate scenario.
watchdog.escrow_monthly_delta.why: It converts a tax scenario into the monthly payment language borrowers and mortgage professionals actually use.
watchdog.escrow_monthly_delta.method: Scenario annual tax minus current annual tax, divided by twelve.
watchdog.escrow_monthly_delta.caution: User-controlled scenario only; it is not a lender disclosure, assessment decision or tax forecast.
